drivingQuestion: Does the mishna's warning against conjecture in capital cases imply conjecture is valid in monetary cases?
outcomeNote: the previous unit's inference (and so its identification with R' Aḥa) is undercut

segments.he: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, עֵד מִפִּי עֵד דְּקָתָנֵי בְּדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת הוּא דְּלָא אָמְרִינַן, הָא בְּדִינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת אָמְרִינַן? וְהָתְנַן: אִם אָמַר ״הוּא אָמַר לִי שֶׁאֲנִי חַיָּיב לוֹ״, ״אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי אָמַר לִי שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב לוֹ״ – לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר ״בְּפָנֵינוּ הוֹדָה לוֹ שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב לוֹ מָאתַיִם זוּז״.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But according to your reasoning,» with regard to «that» which the mishna «teaches,» that the court warns the witnesses not to provide «testimony» based on «hearsay,» should one infer that it is «in» cases of «capital law that we do not say» that testimony based on hearsay is allowed, «but in» cases of «monetary law, we do say» that testimony based on hearsay is allowed? «But didn’t we learn» in a mishna (29a): «If» the witness «said:» The defendant «said to me:» It is true «that I owe» the plaintiff, or if he says: «So-and-so said to me that» the defendant «owes» the plaintiff, the witness «has said nothing,» i.e., his testimony is disregarded. These two statements by witnesses are examples of testimony based on hearsay, yet they are not valid in cases of monetary law. A witness’s testimony is not valid testimony «unless he says,» for example: The defendant «admitted in our presence to» the plaintiff «that he owes him two hundred dinars,» as by admitting the debt in the presence of witnesses he rendered himself liable to pay the amount that he mentioned.

segments.he: אַלְמָא, אַף עַל גַּב דִּפְסִילִי בְּדִינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת, אָמְרִינַן לְהוּ בְּדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת. הָכָא נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דִּפְסִילִי בְּדִינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת, אָמְרִינַן לְהוּ בְּדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת.
segments.en: «Evidently, although» testimony based on hearsay «is invalid in» cases of «monetary law, we tell» the witnesses to be aware of this «in capital law. Here, too,» with regard to testimony based on conjecture, one can say that «although» testimony based on conjecture «is invalid in» cases of «monetary law, we tell» the witnesses to be aware of this «in» cases of «capital law.»
